title: Breaks: 4.5 Hours Then 45 Minutes
whatItIs: Under the assimilated drivers' hours rules, you can drive for no more than 4.5 hours before a break of at least 45 minutes. The break can be split 15 + 30.

keyFacts.text: After no more than 4.5 hours of driving, you MUST take a break of at least 45 minutes, unless you start a rest period.
You can split the 45 minutes: at least 15 minutes first, then at least 30 minutes, spread over the 4.5 hours.

keyFacts: Breaks shorter than 15 minutes don't count towards the 45 minutes.
A break means no driving and no other work: it's only for recuperation.
A qualifying 45-minute break 'wipes the slate clean': a new 4.5-hour driving period starts.
Working time rules can require breaks too, on top of the drivers' hours rules.

rows.label: Split the wrong way: 30, then 15
rows.note: The second part of a split break must be at least 30 minutes.

a.label: Break
points: Short pause for recuperation: 15, 30 or 45 minutes
No driving and no other work

b.label: Rest
points: Long period you can spend as you like
Daily: 11 h (9 h reduced) · Weekly: 45 h (24 h reduced)

onTheTest.question: You've been driving for 4.5 hours. Under the assimilated rules, what's the shortest break you must take now?
onTheTest.why: After no more than 4.5 hours of driving you must take a break of at least 45 minutes, unless you start a rest period.

onTheTest.question: You want to split your 45-minute break. Which pattern is allowed?
onTheTest.why: The first break must be at least 15 minutes and the second at least 30 minutes. Breaks under 15 minutes don't count.

traps: Order matters: 15 then 30 is legal, but 30 then 15 is not.
A 10-minute stop doesn't count towards your 45 minutes.
Loading, unloading or paperwork is other work, not a break.
